After the refresh the live table shows "fwrd72-n3 RD Part A $150.00 25% 1 Bench Supplier $187.50" (price recomputed to $187.50), Part B unchanged at $250.00, and the ticket parts total is now "$437.50" (was $375.00).

The instruction's conditional was answered: the app did NOT refuse. Clicking "Mark Ready" on http://127.0.0.1:4180/#/tickets/t15 (RD-1019) was accepted — status went Draft → Ready — and no error or validation message appeared anywhere (the shared error region #error-region read back empty, and no dialog/toast fired; the click's state diff only swapped the buttons to "Mark Draft" and "Mark Closed"). I verified persistence: the list row after a fresh fetch reads "RD-1019 | fwrd72-n3 RD Bench Ticket | Bench Customer | Ready | 2 | 2026-09-17". The ticket therefore met whatever preconditions the app enforces (it has 2 parts, both cost>0 with markup 25% and a supplier); the exact precondition rules never surfaced in the UI. Related note, flagged as inference from the app's client bundle rather than from the UI: /app.js contains a renderer and comment for a server 409 "Ready precondition" carrying { error, unmet: [...] }, which is how the business rule would be shown if it were unmet — it never fired in this session.

steps.summary: Probed with scratch ticket RD-1020 "fwrd72-n3 RD Scratch Probe Archived RD Scratch Probe" (customer Probe). Mark Ready with no parts was REFUSED with error text "Ticket is not ready" and unmet list: ["A ticket needs at least one part before it can be marked Ready"]; after adding one part (name "Probe part", cost 0, markup 0, no supplier) it was REFUSED again with "Ticket is not ready" + ["Part \"Probe part\" has no supplier"]; setting that part's Supplier to "Probe supplier" was the change that made Mark Ready succeed (status → Ready, no error shown, buttons became Mark Draft/Mark Closed). So the app requires (1) ≥1 part and (2) a supplier on every part — cost 0 / markup 0 did not matter. Note the part form's own hint calls Supplier "Optional. Leave blank if the part has not been sourced yet", which contradicts the precondition. The app exposes no ticket-delete control (only Archive/Unarchive; the sole DELETE in app.js is for parts), so I archived the scratch ticket: it is now absent from the default Tickets list and appears as "RD-1020 | fwrd72-n3 RD Scratch Probe Archived RD Scratch Probe Archived | Probe | Ready | 1 | 2026-09-17" only with "Show archived" ticked.
